argv:
Rewrite the text following the Microsoft writing style.

Sound like a helpful colleague chatting with the reader, not a manual. Use
contractions everywhere they'd naturally occur, address the reader directly as
"you", and reach for everyday words over formal ones. A sentence fragment is
fine when it lands the point — don't force every thought into a full clause.

Open with the single thing the reader most needs to know, then explain. Keep
sentences short and let the page's shape (headings, short paragraphs) do some
of the work.

Use sentence case for any heading. Use the active voice and the present tense.
Tell the reader exactly what to do and what happens next, in a tone that feels
like a quick conversation rather than a document.

Skip jargon, hedging, and anything that talks down to the reader — but don't
skip the personality. A little warmth and a casual aside are welcome.

request.user_prompt:
Rewrite the passage below according to your style instructions.

Output only the rewritten passage. Do not add a preamble, a title, an
explanation, or any commentary about the changes you made.

<passage>
Call me Ishmael. Some years ago—never mind how long precisely—having little or no money in my purse, and nothing particular to interest me on shore, I thought I would sail about a little and see the watery part of the world. It is a way I have of driving off the spleen and regulating the circulation. Whenever I find myself growing grim about the mouth; whenever it is a damp, drizzly November in my soul; whenever I find myself involuntarily pausing before coffin warehouses, and bringing up the rear of every funeral I meet; and especially whenever my hypos get such an upper hand of me, that it requires a strong moral principle to prevent me from deliberately stepping into the street, and methodically knocking people's hats off—then, I account it high time to get to sea as soon as I can. This is my substitute for pistol and ball. With a philosophical flourish Cato throws himself upon his sword; I quietly take to the ship. There is nothing surprising in this. If they but knew it, almost all men in their degree, some time or other, cherish very nearly the same feelings towards the ocean with me.
</passage>

response.text:
Call me Ishmael. So here's the thing: a few years back, with barely a dollar to my name and nothing much keeping me on land, I decided to head out and see the watery part of the world for a while. That's just how I deal with feeling low — it gets my blood moving again.

You know the feeling. Your mouth goes grim, November settles into your soul even when it's not November, and suddenly you're lingering outside coffin shops or tagging along behind funerals that aren't yours. And when things get really bad — when it takes real effort not to walk into the street and start knocking hats off strangers — that's my cue. Time to get to sea, and fast.

Think of it as my version of pistols at dawn. Cato had his sword and his big dramatic exit; I just quietly book passage on a ship. Nothing strange about that, really. Most of us, if we're honest, feel something close to what I feel about the ocean — sooner or later, one way or another.
